text: # Travel and Business Expense Policy ## Travel Reimbursement All business-related travel must be pre-approved by the respective department head. Flights should be booked under economy class unless exceptional circumstances apply. ## Accommodation & Hotel Limits For business travel, hotel expenses are reimbursed up to specific limits. In metro cities, the maximum allowed hotel per night is 6,000 rupees. For non-metro cities, the limit is 3,500 rupees per night. ## Approval Hierarchy - Expenses up to 10,000 rupees require manager approval. - Expenses between 10,000 and 50,000 rupees require approval from the Department Head or Director. - Who approves an expense of 20,000 rupees? An expense of 20,000 rupees must be approved by the Department Head. - Any expense exceeding 50,000 rupees requires VP or Finance Controller sign-off.

# Remote Work and IT Security Policy ## Hybrid Schedule Full-time employees operate on a hybrid schedule. Employees work remotely on Mondays and Fridays. Which days do I work from the office? Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday are designated in-office working days. ## IT Security & Network Access When working remotely, employees must connect via the corporate VPN at all times. Connecting directly to unsecured public wifi networks without activating the VPN is strictly prohibited to safeguard confidential customer and organizational data. Company laptops must not be shared with third parties.

# Leave Policy (sample document for Acme Analytics, a fictional company) All full-time employees receive 24 days of paid annual leave per calendar year. Leave is credited monthly at the rate of 2 days per month. Up to 10 unused days can be carried over to the next year. Any leave above 10 days lapses on 31 December. Sick leave: employees get 12 days of paid sick leave per year. A medical certificate is required if sick leave lasts more than 2 consecutive days. Sick leave cannot be carried over or encashed. Maternity and paternity leave: female employees get 26 weeks of paid maternity leave. Male employees get 2 weeks of paid paternity leave, which must be taken within 3 months of the child's birth.
